categories.title: Greetings and Social Expressions 👋🫂
categories.description: Essential expressions for initiating conversations, showing politeness, and handling everyday social exchanges naturally.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: नमस्ते, आप कैसे हैं?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Namaste, aap kaise hain?
vocabulary.memoryTip: The most versatile Indian greeting. Combine with hands folded at chest level.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: आपकी मदद के लिए धन्यवाद।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Aapki madad ke liye dhanyawad.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Think of 'Dhanya' as blessed — thanking someone leaves a blessed feeling.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: चाय के लिए शुक्रिया!
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Chai ke liye shukriya!
vocabulary.memoryTip: Widely used in daily spoken Hindi as an alternative to Dhanyawad.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: माफ़ कीजिए, क्या मैं यहाँ बैठ सकता हूँ?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Maaf kijiye, kya main yahan baith sakta hoon?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Excuse me, can I sit here?
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Maaf' means forgive/excuse and 'kijiye' is the polite 'please do' form.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: देर हो गई? कोई बात नहीं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Der ho gayi? Koi baat nahin.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Literal breakdown: 'Koi' (Any) + 'baat' (matter) + 'nahin' (not). Nothing to worry about!

vocabulary.exampleHindi: ठीक है, अब अलविदा!
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Theek hai, ab alvida!
vocabulary.memoryTip: Used when parting for a longer duration.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: अलविदा, कल फिर मिलेंगे।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Alvida, kal phir milenge.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Phir' (again) + 'milenge' (we will meet). The standard friendly sign-off.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: कृपया थोड़ा धीरे बोलिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kripya thoda dheere boliye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Place 'Kripya' at the beginning of requests to make them formal and gentle.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: हमारे घर में आपका स्वागत है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Hamare ghar mein aapka swagat hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Seen on signs across India. 'Swagat' directly means welcome.

vocabulary.exampleRoman: Haan, main taiyar hoon.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Simple, short, and nasalized sound 'Haan'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: नहीं, मुझे यह नहीं चाहिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Nahin, mujhe yeh nahin chahiye.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: No, I do not want this.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Pronounced with a slight nasal ending 'Na-heen'.

vocabulary.meaning: All is fine / Everything is good
vocabulary.exampleHindi: चिंता मत कीजिए, सब ठीक है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Chinta mat kijiye, sab theek hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Sab' = All, 'Theek' = Okay, 'Hai' = Is.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: आप बिल्कुल सही कह रहे हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Aap bilkul sahi keh rahe hain.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Rhymes with 'will cool'. Expresses total agreement.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: आपसे मिलकर बहुत खुशी हुई।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Aapse milkar bahut khushi hui.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Khushi' means happiness. Pair with 'Aapse milkar' (meeting you).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: शुभप्रभात! आज का मौसम अच्छा है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Shubh prabhat! Aaj ka mausam achha hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Good morning! Today's weather is good.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Shubh' (Auspicious/Good) + 'Prabhat' (Morning).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: अब मैं सो रहा हूँ, शुभ रात्रि!
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Ab main so raha hoon, shubh ratri!
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am sleeping now, good night!
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Shubh' (Good) + 'Ratri' (Night). Used right before bedtime.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: अरे वाह! यह तो बहुत सुंदर है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Are wah! Yeh to bahut sundar hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Oh wow! This is very beautiful.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Expresses pleasant surprise or appreciation.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: नई नौकरी के लिए बधाई हो!
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Nai naukri ke liye badhai ho!
vocabulary.memoryTip: Used during festivals, birthdays, and professional achievements.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: सब ठीक हो जाएगा, चिंता मत कीजिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Sab theek ho jayega, chinta mat kijiye.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Everything will be fine, do not worry.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Chinta' means worry; 'mat kijiye' means don't do it.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: परीक्षा के लिए आपको शुभकामनाएँ।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Pariksha ke liye aapko shubhkamnayein.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Best wishes to you for the exam.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Shubh' (good) + 'kamnayein' (wishes).

conversation.speaker: Rohan
conversation.hindi: नमस्ते शर्मा जी! आप कैसे हैं?
conversation.roman: Namaste Sharma ji! Aap kaise hain?
conversation.meaning: Hello Mr. Sharma! How are you?

conversation.speaker: Sharma Ji
conversation.hindi: नमस्ते रोहन! मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद। आपसे मिलकर खुशी हुई।
conversation.roman: Namaste Rohan! Main theek hoon, dhanyawad. Aapse milkar khushi hui.
conversation.meaning: Hello Rohan! I am fine, thank you. Pleased to meet you.

conversation.speaker: Sharma Ji
conversation.hindi: हाँ, बिल्कुल सब ठीक है। अब मैं चलता हूँ, फिर मिलेंगे!
conversation.roman: Haan, bilkul sab theek hai. Ab main chalta hoon, phir milenge!
conversation.meaning: Yes, absolutely fine. I'll take my leave now, see you again!

categories.title: People and Relationships 👨🏻‍👩🏻‍👦🏻‍👦🏻
categories.description: Vocabulary for identifying family members, social relations, colleagues, and addressing people with appropriate respect in India.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: यहाँ बहुत सारे लोग हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Yahan bahut sare log hain.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Think of a crowd where many people 'lodge' together.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: अमित मेरा सबसे अच्छा दोस्त है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Amit mera sabse achha dost hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Commonly used word across India for male or female friends.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरा परिवार दिल्ली में रहता है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mera parivar Delhi mein rehta hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Sounds like 'pair-i-var'. Central aspect of Indian culture.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरे माता-पिता गाँव में हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mere mata-pita gaon mein hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My parents are in the village.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Mata = Mother, Pita = Father. Joined naturally together.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: माँ ने बहुत स्वादिष्ट खाना बनाया है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Maa ne bahut swadisht khana banaya hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Mother has cooked very delicious food.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Universal soft sound 'Maa'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: पिताजी दफ़्तर गए हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Pitaji daftar gaye hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Father has gone to the office.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Always add '-ji' after Pita to show traditional respect.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरा एक छोटा भाई है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mera ek chhota bhai hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Used both for actual brothers and informally for male peers ('bro').

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरी बहन कॉलेज में पढ़ती है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Meri behan college mein padhti hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Pronounced like 'Bay-hen'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: बेटा, यहाँ आओ।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Beta, yahan aao.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Elders often address younger people affectionately as 'Beta'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: उनकी बेटी डॉक्टर है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Unki beti doctor hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Notice the gender vowel change: Beta (masculine) -> Beti (feminine).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरे पति बैंक में काम करते हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mere pati bank mein kaam karte hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My husband works in a bank.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Short two-syllable word.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: उनकी पत्नी एक शिक्षिका हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Unki patni ek shikshika hain.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Pair with Pati: Pati (husband) & Patni (wife).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: वह मेरे नए सहकर्मी हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Vah mere naye sahkarmi hain.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Sah' (Co/Together) + 'Karmi' (Worker).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: हमारे पड़ोसी बहुत मददगार हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Hamare padosi bahut madadgar hain.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Think of the area nearby as 'pados'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: बच्चे पार्क में खेल रहे हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Bachhe park mein khel rahe hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Children are playing in the park.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Singular is 'Bachha' (child), plural is 'Bachhe' (children).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: कल हमारे घर रिश्तेदार आ रहे हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kal hamare ghar rishtedaar aa rahe hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Relatives are coming to our house tomorrow.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Rishta' means relation/connection.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: भारतीय संस्कृति में अतिथि को भगवान माना जाता है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Bharatiya sanskriti mein atithi ko bhagwan mana jata hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: In Indian culture, a guest is considered equivalent to God.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Derived from classical Sanskrit, widely used in formal hospitality.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: कार्यालय के मालिक बहुत दयालु हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Karyalay ke malik bahut dayalu hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The office owner/boss is very kind.
vocabulary.memoryTip: The person in charge of the business or property.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: दुकान पर एक नया ग्राहक आया है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Dukan par ek naya grahak aaya hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A new customer has come to the shop.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Essential word for shopping and business interactions.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: शहर में किसी अजनबी पर तुरंत भरोसा मत करो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Shehar mein kisi ajnabee par turant bharosa mat karo.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do not trust a stranger immediately in the city.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Someone unknown to you.

conversation.speaker: Neha
conversation.hindi: अमित, क्या यह आपके परिवार की फ़ोटो है?
conversation.roman: Amit, kya yeh aapke parivar ki photo hai?
conversation.meaning: Amit, is this a photo of your family?

conversation.speaker: Amit
conversation.hindi: हाँ, इसमें मेरे पिताजी, माँ और मेरी बहन हैं।
conversation.roman: Haan, ismein mere pitaji, maa aur meri behan hain.
conversation.meaning: Yes, in this are my father, mother, and my sister.

conversation.speaker: Neha
conversation.hindi: और यह पास में कौन खड़े हैं?
conversation.roman: Aur yeh paas mein kaun khade hain?
conversation.meaning: And who is this standing nearby?

conversation.speaker: Amit
conversation.hindi: यह मेरा सबसे अच्छा दोस्त और मेरा पड़ोसी, विकास है।
conversation.roman: Yeh mera sabse achha dost aur mera padosi, Vikas hai.
conversation.meaning: This is my best friend and my neighbor, Vikas.

categories.title: Common Everyday Objects 📦
categories.description: Everyday tangible items found around carrying bags, desk space, electronics, and daily essentials.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: यह क्या चीज़ है?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Yeh kya cheez hai?
vocabulary.memoryTip: Easy to remember because it sounds like the food 'cheese'!

vocabulary.exampleHindi: अपना सामान यहाँ रखिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Apna samaan yahan rakhiye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Collective term for all personal belongings.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरा फ़ोन कहाँ है?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mera phone kahan hai?
vocabulary.memoryTip: Loan word used universally in spoken Hindi.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: घर की चाबी मेज़ पर है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Ghar ki chaabi mez par hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The house key is on the table.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Think of starting a car: turn the 'Chaabi'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरा बैग बहुत भारी है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mera bag bahut bhaari hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Widely used Hinglish word alongside Hindi 'Thaila'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैं एक नई किताब पढ़ रहा हूँ।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Main ek nai kitaab padh raha hoon.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am reading a new book.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Rhymes with 'Key-taab'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: क्या आपके पास एक कलम है?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kya aapke paas ek kalam hai?
vocabulary.memoryTip: Also commonly referred to simply as 'Pen' in daily office Hindi.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: इस कागज़ पर अपना नाम लिखिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Is kaagaz par apna naam likhiye.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Write your name on this paper.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Think of important legal or official papers.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरी घड़ी में पाँच बजे हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Meri ghadi mein paanch baje hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is 5 o'clock in my watch.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Sounds like 'Ghar-ee'. Measures time.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरा चश्मा कहाँ रखा है?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mera chashma kahan rakha hai?
vocabulary.memoryTip: Think of 'eye glasses'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: क्या आपके पास नक़द पैसे हैं?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kya aapke paas naqad paise hain?
vocabulary.memoryTip: General term used for money or currency in Hindi.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैंने अपना बटुआ जेब में रखा है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Maine apna batua jeb mein rakha hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have kept my wallet in the pocket.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Small pocket pouch used for carrying money.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: पानी की बोतल ठंडी है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Paani ki botal thandi hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Sounds very similar to the English word 'Bottle'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: बारिश हो रही है, छाता ले जाओ।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Baarish ho rahi hai, chhaata le jaao.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is raining, take an umbrella.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Provides 'chhaaya' (shade/cover) from rain and sun.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मिठाई का डिब्बा मेज़ पर रख दो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mithai ka dibba mez par rakh do.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Keep the sweet box on the table.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Used for lunchboxes (Tiffin dibba) or shipping boxes.

conversation.speaker: Priya
conversation.hindi: सुनो, क्या तुमने मेरा बैग देखा?
conversation.roman: Suno, kya tumne mera bag dekha?
conversation.meaning: Listen, did you see my bag?

conversation.speaker: Raj
conversation.hindi: हाँ, बैग मेज़ पर है। उसमें क्या है?
conversation.roman: Haan, bag mez par hai. Usmein kya hai?
conversation.meaning: Yes, the bag is on the table. What is in it?

conversation.speaker: Priya
conversation.hindi: उसमें मेरी किताब, कलम और घर की चाबी है।
conversation.roman: Usmein meri kitaab, kalam aur ghar ki chaabi hai.
conversation.meaning: In it are my book, pen, and house key.

conversation.speaker: Raj
conversation.hindi: और तुम्हारा फ़ोन और बटुआ कहाँ है?
conversation.roman: Aur tumhara phone aur batua kahan hai?
conversation.meaning: And where are your phone and wallet?

categories.title: Home and Household 🏠
categories.description: Vocabulary associated with house spaces, furniture, household items, and basic living environments.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरा घर बहुत बड़ा है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mera ghar bahut bada hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Core word for home. Expresses warmth and personal living place.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: यह कमरा साफ और हवादार है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Yeh kamra saaf aur hawadaar hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This room is clean and airy.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Think of camera = room (originated from Latin camera/vault).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: माँ रसोई में खाना बना रही हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Maa rasoi mein khana bana rahi hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Mother is cooking food in the kitchen.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Rasa' = taste/juice; where tasty food is made.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: कृपया दरवाज़ा बंद कर दीजिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kripya darwaza band kar dijiye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Sounds like 'Dar-waa-zaa'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: खिड़की खोल दो, ताज़ी हवा आएगी।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Khidki khol do, taazi hawa aayegi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Open the window, fresh air will come.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Click-clack sound of opening a 'Khidki'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: चाय का कप मेज़ पर रख दो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Chai ka cup mez par rakh do.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Keep the tea cup on the table.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Short one-syllable word 'Mez'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: इस कुर्सी पर बैठिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Is kursi par baithiye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Standard word for chair in home or office.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: बिस्तर साफ और आरामदायक है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Bistar saaf aur aaramdayak hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bed is clean and comfortable.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Where you stretch out ('star' / spread out).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: गर्मी है, पंखा चला दो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Garmi hai, pankha chala do.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is hot, turn on the fan.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Pankh' means feather/wing; a fan spins like wings.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: कमरे की बत्ती जला दो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kamre ki batti jala do.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Also referred to as 'Light' in daily spoken Hinglish.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: बिस्तर पर नई चादर बिछा दो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Bistar par nai chaadar bichha do.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Spread a new bedsheet on the bed.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Covers the bed like a shield.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मुझे एक और तकिया चाहिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mujhe ek aur takiya chahiye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Soft cushion for sleeping.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: कपड़े अलमारी में रख दो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kapde almari mein rakh do.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Put the clothes in the cupboard.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Cognate with English 'almirah'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: दरवाज़े पर ताला लगा दो।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Darwaze par taala laga do.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Put a lock on the door.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Chaabi (Key) opens the Taala (Lock).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: आज हम घर की सफ़ाई करेंगे।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Aaj hum ghar ki safai karenge.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Today we will clean the house.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Saaf' means clean; 'Safai' is the act of cleaning.

conversation.speaker: Suresh
conversation.hindi: यह आपका नया घर बहुत सुंदर है!
conversation.roman: Yeh aapka naya ghar bahut sundar hai!
conversation.meaning: This new house of yours is very beautiful!

conversation.speaker: Anil
conversation.hindi: धन्यवाद! आइए, इस कमरे में बैठिए।
conversation.roman: Dhanyawad! Aaiye, is kamre mein baithiye.
conversation.meaning: Thank you! Come, sit in this room.

conversation.speaker: Anil
conversation.hindi: माफ़ कीजिए, मैं अभी पंखा चलाता हूँ और खिड़की खोलता हूँ।
conversation.roman: Maaf kijiye, main abhi pankha chalata hoon aur khidki kholta hoon.
conversation.meaning: Sorry, I will turn on the fan right now and open the window.

categories.title: Time of Day and Daily Schedule 🕓
categories.description: Essential vocabulary for tracking time, daily routine periods, meal times, and scheduling.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैं सुबह जल्दी उठता/उठती हूँ।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Main subah jaldi uthta/uthti hoon.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I wake up early in the morning.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Starts the day with fresh energy.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: हम दोपहर में मिलते हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Hum dopahar mein milte hain.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Middle of the day when the sun is right above.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: दोपहर का खाना तैयार है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Dopahar ka khana taiyar hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Literal breakdown: 'Dopahar' (noon/afternoon) + 'ka khana' (food of).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: हम शाम को सैर करने जाते हैं।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Hum shaam ko sair karne jaate hain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We go for a walk in the evening.
vocabulary.memoryTip: When daylight begins to fade into sunset.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: रात का खाना बहुत स्वादिष्ट था।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Raat ka khana bahut swadisht tha.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Used for nighttime and late hours.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: क्या आपने रात का खाना खा लिया?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kya aapne raat ka khana kha liya?
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Raat' (night) + 'ka khana' (food).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: अभी क्या समय हुआ है?
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Abhi kya samay hua hai?
vocabulary.memoryTip: Universal word for time or duration.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मेरे पास अभी वक्त नहीं है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Mere paas abhi waqt nahin hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I don't have time right now.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Commonly used alternative to Samay in casual spoken Hindi.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: आज मौसम बहुत अच्छा है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Aaj mausam bahut achha hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Today the weather is very good.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Refers to the current day.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैं कल कार्यालय आऊँगा/आऊँगी।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Main kal karyalay aaunga/aaungi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will come to the office tomorrow.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Context determines whether Kal means yesterday or tomorrow.

vocabulary.meaning: Day before yesterday / Day after tomorrow
vocabulary.exampleHindi: हमारी मीटिंग परसों है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Hamari meeting parson hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Our meeting is the day after tomorrow.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Extends one step beyond 'Kal'.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: वह रोज़ हिंदी का अभ्यास करता/करती है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Vah roz Hindi ka abhyas karta/karti hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Means routine or daily repetition.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: यह काम तुरंत कीजिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Yeh kaam turant kijiye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Done without delay.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: माफ़ कीजिए, मुझे देर हो गई।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Maaf kijiye, mujhe der ho gayi.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Opposite of jaldi (early/fast).

vocabulary.exampleHindi: कृपया जल्दी आइए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Kripya jaldi aaiye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Used to tell someone to hurry up.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: यह काम एक घंटे में पूरा हो जाएगा।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Yeh kaam ek ghante mein pura ho jayega.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This work will be completed in one hour.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Measures duration in sixty-minute blocks.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: बस पाँच मिनट रुकिए।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Bas paanch minute rukiye.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Borrowed directly from English for short time intervals.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैं बस एक सेकंड में आता हूँ।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Main bas ek second mein aata hoon.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will come in just a second.
vocabulary.memoryTip: The shortest common unit of time.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: वह सुबह-सुबह सैर पर जाती है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Vah subah-subah sair par jaati hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: She goes for a walk early in the morning.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Repeating a word emphasizes its intensity or immediacy.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: दोपहर के समय बहुत धूप होती है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Dopahar ke samay bahut dhoop hoti hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is very sunny at noon.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Specifies the peak heat hours of the day.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: हम शाम को चाय पिएँगे।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Hum shaam ko chai piyenge.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We will drink tea in the evening.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Adding 'ko' denotes the timeframe during which an action occurs.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: वह आधी रात तक जाग रहा था।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Vah aadhi raat tak jaag raha tha.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Aadhi' means half, so 'half night' = midnight.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: सच्चाई की हमेशा जीत होती है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Sachchai ki hamesha jeet hoti hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Indicates permanent or constant frequency.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैं कभी-कभी कॉफ़ी पीता हूँ।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Main kabhi-kabhi coffee peeta hoon.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Kabhi' means ever/sometimes; repeating it means occasionally.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: वह अक्सर देर से आता है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Vah aksar der se aata hai.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Describes habitual or recurrent actions.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैं ऐसा कभी नहीं कहूँगा।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Main aisa kabhi nahin kahunga.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will never say such a thing.
vocabulary.memoryTip: 'Kabhi' (ever) + 'nahin' (not) = never.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: मैंने हाल ही में एक किताब पढ़ी है।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Maine haal hi mein ek kitaab padhi hai.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have recently read a book.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Refers to events that happened in the near past.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: अचानक बारिश शुरू हो गई।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Achanak baarish shuru ho gayi.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Describes an unexpected occurrence without prior notice.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: हम अगली मीटिंग में मिलेंगे।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Hum agli meeting mein milenge.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We will meet in the next meeting.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Points forward to the coming time or item.

vocabulary.exampleHindi: पिछला हफ्ता बहुत व्यस्त था।
vocabulary.exampleRoman: Pichhla hafta bahut vyast tha.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The previous week was very busy.
vocabulary.memoryTip: Points backward to what has passed.
